workWithMe.metaDescription: Start a conversation about coaching. A short enquiry form, read personally by Fareed. No intake questionnaire, no clinical history, no obligation.

intro.title: Interested in working together?
intro.lede: The first step is a short conversation. Tell me your name, an email address, and — if you want to — a sentence or two about what you are navigating. I read every message myself and reply personally.
intro.note: This is not a booking system. There is nothing to schedule here, and nothing to pay.

how.title: What happens after you send this

steps.name: I read it
steps.body: Your message comes straight to me. No assistant, no funnel, no automated sequence.

steps.name: I reply
steps.body: You will hear back from me personally, usually within a few days, at the email address you provide.

steps.name: We talk
steps.body: If it seems worth exploring, we arrange a short introductory conversation — by video or phone — at no cost.

steps.name: You decide
steps.body: If the work is a fit and the timing is right, we agree on a structure. If not, that is a completely acceptable outcome.

form.title: Start a conversation
form.lede: Three fields. Please share only what you are comfortable putting in an email — this is an enquiry, not an intake form.

message.label: What would you like to work on?
message.hint: Optional. A sentence or two is plenty — no need for history or detail.

form.consent: I will use your message only to reply to you about coaching. Nothing is added to a mailing list, and nothing is shared with anyone else.
form.privacyNote: Please do not include medical, diagnostic, or psychiatric information. This form is not monitored for urgent or crisis support. If you need immediate help, contact a crisis line or emergency services.

scope.title: Scope of practice
scope.lede: Coaching and psychotherapy are different professions with different training, and it is worth being explicit about where this work sits. This is not legal boilerplate — it is the boundary that makes the work safe.

supports.title: What coaching supports
supports.intro: Coaching focuses on strengthening the capacities that allow you to live and relate more intentionally. That may include:
items: Clarifying personal values and life direction
Recognising behavioural patterns that no longer serve you
Building emotional awareness and regulation skills
Creating practical structures that support your goals
supports.outro: Coaching is forward-facing. Past experience may be acknowledged, but the focus of the work is on how you want to live going forward and what capacities will support that.

doesNot.title: What coaching does not provide
doesNot.intro: Life coaching and somatic coaching are not psychotherapy and do not replace mental health care. As a coach, I do not:
items: Provide psychotherapy, trauma therapy, or crisis counselling
Prescribe medication or offer medical treatment
Give advice that requires clinical training I do not hold
doesNot.outro: If you are seeking assessment, diagnosis, or treatment for a mental health concern, that belongs with a licensed clinician — a psychologist, psychiatrist, or registered psychotherapist.

referral.title: When I may suggest something else
referral.intro: Sometimes the most useful thing I can do is recommend a different kind of support. If what you bring would be better served by clinical care, I will say so directly.
referral.outro: That is not a judgement about you, and it is not a failure of the coaching. It is how I keep this work responsible. Coaching can sit alongside therapy; it does not replace it.
